anomalies.obs: On the mcu.kicad_sch sheet (top right), the USB-C receptacle J10 data pins are wired so that NET0009 carries both a D+ pin (A6) and a D- pin (B7), and NET0010 carries both a D- pin (A7) and a D+ pin (B6). The two label boxes sit at the two D- rows (A7, B7) and the D+ rows (A6, B6) are jumpered into those same two nets, producing a visible wire crossing. NET0009 also drives U2 pin 27 (GPIO19/USB_D+) and NET0010 drives U2 pin 26 (GPIO18/USB_D-).
anomalies.expected: Standard USB-C wiring (and the spec's USB-C programming interface) requires the two D+ pins (A6, B6) to share one net and the two D- pins (A7, B7) to share a separate net, so the ESP32-C3 USB_D+ and USB_D- lines remain a proper differential pair. Instead D+ and D- are shorted together on each net.

evidence.quote: mcu.kicad_sch top-right: J10 A7->NET0010, B7->NET0009, A6->NET0009, B6->NET0010; U2 pin27 GPIO19/USB_D+->NET0009, pin26 GPIO18/USB_D-->NET0010
Accepts power from either a 12 V barrel jack ... or USB-C 5 V (J12, logic/programming supply) ... USB-C CC1/CC2 pins go through R1/R7 (5.1 kΩ each) to GND

anomalies.impact: The USB-C differential pair is shorted (D+ tied to D-), so the ESP32-C3 will fail to enumerate over USB; programming and USB serial communication are broken.

parsed.summary: The build's topology otherwise matches the specification (power mux, buck, smart high-side heater switch, three shared-SPI MAX31855 channels, CC pulldowns), but on the MCU sheet the USB-C D+/D- data pins are cross-connected so that each net carries one D+ and one D-, shorting the differential pair and breaking USB.
